subject: qilin
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: qilin, scaled hooved chimera with antlers and cloud mane.
Style: high-fantasy anime.
reasoning:
I'm sketching out a design for a quadruped qilin creature with a dragon-style head, antlers, cloud-like mane, fire tail, and scale textures, planning to build it piece by piece using limb IK for the legs and jaw articulation for the head.

Now I'm working out the skeleton and body proportions in detail—placing hip, spine, neck, and head joints at specific heights, then figuring out how to sweep a body mesh along the spine chain with varying radii for shape.

For the head I'm setting a slight forward-up tilt direction and using local coordinate words like forward, up, and left/right for positioning facial features, then building the skull as a scaled sphere and the snout as a tapered frustum box extending forward from the head joint.

Continuing to layer parts: a jaw joint parented to the head for the lower jaw's frustum box, a small sphere for the nose, cone shapes for teeth, and eyes placed as decals on the skull surface using a hit-based positioning helper, mirroring everything for symmetry.

Now I'm sketching antlers by sprouting curved sweep paths from hit points on the skull at specific azimuth and elevation angles, building the main beam using local offsets along left/up/back axes to curve upward and backward from the head.

I'm planning cloud texture cards scattered along the neck, head, chest, fetlocks, and tail using swirling teal/white gradient shapes, with fire-like glowing cloud cards for the tail. For coloring, I'm settling on a qilin-inspired palette: gold-ochre scaled body, cream belly, white/aqua cloud mane, jade-gold antlers, gold hooves, and violet eyes, all rendered in a cel-shaded anime style.

Now I'm working out the leg rigging -- setting shoulder and hip joint positions for front and hind legs, then defining segment lengths and bend directions to get a natural digitigrade stance with knees and elbows bending correctly.

Building the leg chain function with four joint names mapped to the segment points, tapering thickness toward the foot, and adding a cylindrical hoof capping the bottom of each leg near ground level.

Now setting up the hips joint as the root for hind legs and spine attachment, then tuning torso radius curves for chest-to-rump coverage so the body silhouette flows naturally along the spine bones.

I'm shaping the torso path with four points stretching from the shoulders to haunches, adjusting the elliptical radius profile for width and height. Then I'm sprouting a tail chain off the hips with a catmull curve sweeping up and back, tapering its radius and adding fiery cloud cards at the tip for a flame-like effect.

Now I'm placing flame-textured cards along the tail using sampled frames from the sweep, angling them with lean and flow parameters, plus a bigger tuft card at the very end, then applying glow to the whole array. For the mane, I'm scattering cloud-textured cards across the upward-facing neck surface, filtering by normal direction to keep them on top.

I'm extending this with smaller back scatter cards, cheek ruffs, and a hanging beard made from jaw-aligned frames with a downward lean, all using cloud textures in white and teal tints. For the eye, I'm planning to use an anime-style iris decal placed on the skull surface at a specific azimuth angle around a defined center point.

Now I'm sketching out the rest of the creature: curved bezier whiskers sweeping from the muzzle in gold, leaf-shaped extruded ears, a glowing pearl at the chest, and a cel-shaded body paint combining countershaded scales with a cream belly overlay.

Next I'm adding a flank emblem — a swirl rune decal placed on the body surface using a hit point computed from the body sweep orientation. For the cloud texture, I'm drawing an SVG swirl plume shape, a tapering flame-like curl rooted at the card's bottom.

Writing cloud SVG path...

Still setting up the jaw and head joint positions...

Adding fangs as small cones, then scattering small cards on the skull sides for cheek ruff detail. I'm sketching out the part-building helper and importing toon-shading utilities like cel shading and anime eyes, then designing the ear as an extruded pointed leaf shape tilted outward from the head.

Still writing ear geometry...

Now I'm handling null hit cases with non-null assertions, placing an emblem decal on the flank, and scattering mane cards across the neck with filtered normals for a chunky double-sided look, tuning card size, lean, flow, and bend parameters, then starting a similar scatter for chest hair based on forward-facing normals.

Generating ring and card code for the fetlocks...

Setting hoof placement by targeting the leg chain tip at the ground height.
